issue.title: Bug: test_pfc_frames_not_counted_as_rx_ok fails due to long run time and inadequate assertion

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

mellanox

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug
The bug is introduced by https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/25741. On some of Mellanox devices(SN2700), when there are multiple active interfaces, the test will inject PFC pause to each one of them and to each priority sequentially, which lead to ~30min test time. During this window, the RX_OK keeps increasing and exceeds the margin 2000.

### Steps to Reproduce
Need to run this test on some slow devices or devices with multiple active interfaces(For example Mellanox SN2700). The longer the test runs, the test is more likely to fail, because the margin is fixed.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

The test verify that the RX_OK and RX_DRP are not increased greatly due to pfc injection, but use a fixed number of margin 2000, and the condition is RX_OK < margin and RX_DRP < margin. My question is, how is the margin determined? From our failure, it looks like these 3000+ RX_OK are not from PFC injection. Shall we modify the test to choose the margin wisely? Or we need to optimize the assertion logic so that it can identify that the RX_OK delta and RX_DRP delta really come from PFC injection?

### Relevant log output

```shell
AssertionError: PFC frames were counted as RX_OK or RX_DRP beyond the allowed margin of 2000 on the following interfaces [(intf, rx_ok_delta, rx_drp_delta)]: [('Ethernet40', 3233, 0), ('Ethernet56', 3231, 0), ('Ethernet64', 3166, 0), ('Ethernet68', 3158, 0), ('Ethernet72', 3159, 0), ('Ethernet76', 3162, 0), ('Ethernet80', 3157, 0), ('Ethernet84', 3156, 0), ('Ethernet88', 3159, 0), ('Ethernet92', 3169, 0), ('Ethernet96', 3164, 0), ('Ethernet100', 3169, 0), ('Ethernet104', 3168, 0), ('Ethernet108', 3157, 0), ('Ethernet112', 3164, 0), ('Ethernet116', 3166, 0), ('Ethernet120', 3159, 0), ('Ethernet124', 3169, 0)]
```

resolution.title: Fix background RX_OK issue with new PFC counter test
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Fixes #26831

Some devices have large amounts of background traffic on a large port scale. The PFC frame injection takes a long time to perform, causing background traffic to accumulate.
Fix by instead selecting a random port to test.

Performance comparison for Cisco-8223 device with 28 ports active:
- Original version (loop on all ports but read once): 133s
- With a single loop across all ports clearing each time: 322s
- Possible 8-threaded implementation: 87s
- Randomly selecting a port: 60 s
